result.rationale: The diff shows `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in embed.js — a substring-containment origin check. Since discourseUrl is a full URL string, any origin that is a prefix of it (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.co' vs 'http://eviltrout.com') passes, and even unrelated origins contained anywhere in the URL string pass. This allows arbitrary embedding pages to send 'discourse-resize' messages manipulating the iframe height. The mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff line.

judged_text: The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of exact origin equality. Any origin that is a string prefix of the forum URL — e.g. a site registered at eviltrout.co when discourseUrl is http://eviltrout.com — passes the check and can drive discourse-resize messages, letting third-party content on the embedding page collapse or blow out the comments iframe height.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring containment check, not an exact-origin match. If `e.origin` is a prefix of `discourseUrl` (e.g., `http://eviltrout.co` vs `http://eviltrout.com`), `indexOf` returns 0 and the check passes, allowing a non-Discourse origin to send `discourse-resize` messages and control the iframe height.
